content: If you are currently taking loracarbef, it is important to contact your doctor to discuss transitioning to an alternative treatment. Loracarbef is an antibiotic prescribed to treat specific bacterial infections, including pneumonia, bronchitis, and infections of the ear, nose, skin, throat, and urinary tract. It is not effective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. In some cases, loracarbef may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Loracarbef is available in capsule and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken once daily or every 12 hours (twice daily) for a duration of 7 to 14 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take loracarbef exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Shake the liquid form well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Continue taking loracarbef even if you feel better, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking loracarbef, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to loracarbef, cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cefadroxil or cephalexin), penicillin, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), probenecid, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, colitis, or stomach problems. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking loracarbef, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking loracarbef. Take loracarbef at least one hour before or two hours after meals. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Loracarbef may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, or mild skin rash. If you experience severe side effects, such as a severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, or a vaginal infection, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store loracarbef in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep the capsules and liquid at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store in the bathroom). Do not freeze the medication. Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to loracarbef. If you have diabetes, consult your doctor before changing your diet or medication dosage. Use Clinistix or TesTape (not Clinitest) to test your urine for sugar while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the course of loracarbef, contact your doctor.
